subject: arcadeCabinet
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a synthwave-style 1980s arcade cabinet as a single static TS module, sizing it realistically at about 1.8m tall facing +Z, and thinking through how to build the side silhouette and main shapes efficiently with the builder's box and extrude primitives.

Sketching the side profile coordinates...

I'm planning the side art as a synthwave sun with cutout stripes and mountain triangles, then listing out the remaining parts: side extrudes, a back panel box, and a kick plate box at the front with their dimensions and positions.

For the next section I'm sketching the coin door area with glowing slot mechanisms and a neon kickplate strip, plus the slanted control panel slab positioned and angled against the cabinet's front lip, nudging the box dimensions to roughly match the side profile.

Now I'm adding the dual joysticks with colored ball tops, side buttons in magenta/cyan/yellow with glow effects, and sketching the tilted monitor bezel leaning back slightly above the control panel.

Working through the rotation math, I confirm the normal tilts upward correctly as the screen leans back, so I nudge the screen's position slightly along that normal and verify the bezel's top and bottom edges still line up properly with the surrounding side panels.

Checking the side profile, the bezel box sits mostly inside the cabinet's slope and only sticks out a few millimeters, which is acceptable since it's meant to read as a bezel edge. I decide to thicken the bezel box toward the back so its front face aligns closer to the screen plane, then plan to add an outer bezel frame with a subtle neon edge glow before drawing the screen content itself using an SVG texture.

Now I'm working out the marquee header: a box positioned above the screen with a glowing front panel textured with "ASTRO GRID" text, plus thin neon trim boxes framing it in cyan and a top cap panel in magenta, making sure the dark fill box and frame pieces line up with the cabinet's profile curve between the marquee and screen area.

I'm also filling the gap between the bezel top and marquee underside with a small front panel box, then adding the coin door section below the control panel -- a darker recessed plate with glowing coin slots in yellow and red tones and a "25¢" label for detail.

Then I'm working out the lower lip under the control panel where the cabinet slants outward, approximating it with an angled front box, and setting up the back panel to run straight up before slanting into the angled top deck near the top of the cabinet.

For the neon trim, I'm considering different approaches to get a glowing border effect — either extruding a slightly larger outline behind each side panel, or layering a second scaled-down inset panel in a contrasting color to simulate a border inset with a gradient look.

Using a hexagonal tube section with small radius positioned at the outer face so it's partially embedded in the side. Now thinking about side art placement, maybe a sun disc on the lower back area within the inner panel.

Writing sun gradient layers...

Thinking about whether to add mountains below the sun—considering dark purple triangular silhouettes with cyan outlines and maybe small snow caps, though I might skip extra elements like palm trees to keep it simple.

Since the extrusion direction runs along z, both sides render symmetrically with the sun in the same spot, so no mirroring is needed. I'm adding front corner trim strips with magenta glow, a cyan marquee frame, and a dark kick plate with a magenta glow strip near the bottom.

Now I'm sketching the control panel: a deep purple surface with cyan neon line accents, "1P"/"2P" lettering, two glowing start buttons (red and blue), and decorative stripe boxes. I'm also placing the joysticks with tilted shafts and red/cyan balls, plus positioning the surrounding buttons for each player side.

Still working out button and joystick placement...

Now I'm sketching the marquee artwork as an SVG with a dark gradient backdrop, bold chrome-style "ASTRO GRID" lettering, sun rays, and scattered stars. For the screen art, I'm designing a retro synthwave scene with a gradient sky fading into a sun, horizon stripes, and a perspective grid floor converging toward a vanishing point.

Still writing styles...

I'm deciding to skip extra embellishments like a floor underglow strip and leg levelers, keeping the base profile simple and flush with the ground, while still planning minor coin-door and cabinet detailing.

Defining the extrude outline points...

Still writing sweep logic...

Still placing scene elements...

Still positioning mountain peaks and converging rods...

Now I'm shifting to using absolute yz coordinates for the outlines and sun bands rather than relative positioning, then writing the rod helper calls with glow colors for the neon effect. Next I'm generating the screen texture SVG with a gradient background for the retro CRT look.

Writing SVG code...

Still styling the marquee title...

Now I'm working out the screen's position relative to the bezel, computing the offset using the tilt angle so the plane sits just in front of the bezel surface, and checking that the bezel's top edge lines up near the marquee without overlapping the control panel.

The screen plane dimensions (.48 x .40) match the intended aspect ratio of the arcade monitor content, fitting nicely within the bezel's inner border. I'm deciding to keep the bezel dark and skip adding an extra highlight frame for simplicity, then moving on to positioning the marquee art plane.

Now I'm figuring out the marquee box and glowing frame bars, placing cyan accent bars at the top and bottom edges around the marquee artwork and sketching a magenta stripe for the cap, working through the coordinates to align everything along the z-axis.

Then I'm working out the coin door details: a dark plate on the kick panel's front face, with small coin slot cutouts flanked by yellow glow bezels and black slot openings, placing each piece precisely by offsetting their z-depth so they sit flush against the front surface.

Below that I'm adding a lower kickboard section with a darker box and a thin magenta neon strip, then tackling the slanted lower cabinet front -- building a tilted box between the kickboard and control panel to fill that angled profile segment.

Still placing panel geometry...

Adding neon edge strips at the front corners, then considering extra details like speaker grilles, side-art accents, and a power cord sweeping from the back toward the floor as a small finishing touch.

Now I'm adding back-panel vent slots and a back door accent strip, plus the back panel box itself to close off the interior with the sides and front kick.

Checking the upper region is fully enclosed too—marquee, bezel, and back panel cover the gaps so nothing is visible inside from any camera angle. Now I'm writing the final metadata (name, description) and the box helper function to start generating the actual code.
